headline: Bradesco ADRs jump 15% as Brazil's market soars on talk of its chairman becoming finance minister
summary: Bradesco's US-listed shares rose 15.2% to $2.80, catching up with a big rally in São Paulo while US markets were closed for Thanksgiving: the Ibovespa jumped 6.1% on 26 November on speculation that Luiz Trabuco, chairman of Bradesco's board, would become Brazil's finance minister.
why: President Lula had met Trabuco earlier in the week, and reports that he could take over the finance ministry were read by investors as a sign of a more market-friendly fiscal policy. In São Paulo, Bradesco rose 11.6% and Banco do Brasil 12.6% on 26 November, after gains on 25 November on the same reports; the US-listed shares reflect both days because Wall Street was shut on Thursday.

The rally came days after the government signed a fiscal adjustment law targeting a primary budget surplus of 0.5% of GDP from 2027, which many investors had called insufficient, and reports that a second step aimed at mandatory spending was being prepared. Bank shares were the main beneficiaries because lower government borrowing needs would ease pressure on interest rates; no appointment had been confirmed when the shares moved.

src.title: Trading Economics: Brazil stocks soar on finance minister speculation (Nov 26, 2026)
